sec-2159134.summary: Atmos Clinic is a seed-stage New York City startup, founded in 2026, that is building an AI-native care platform. It has chat-based virtual primary care, an employer-sponsored healthcare expense card, and a marketplace of transparently priced local services. One aggregator says it targets small employers at about $50 per employee per month. That figure came from a search summary and I did not confirm it on a page. The company appears to be pre-launch.
sec-2159134.fit: Atmos Clinic is a well-funded, brand-new telehealth and primary care company with a 1-10 person team. It is hiring a founding product engineer to build its React Native/Expo app. It needs patient-facing health data, AI and consent infrastructure. Connect's FHIR, HIPAA-ready consent and audit, lab-PDF AI and medication workflow could let it launch sooner than building that stack itself. The risk is that it is building its own AI-native platform in-house, and its founders come from Ambience Healthcare and Oscar Health, so they may prefer to build. The $8 per member per month price may also clash with a roughly $50 per employee per month model.
pain_points: A tiny team (1-10 people) has to build a mobile app plus a HIPAA-grade FHIR data layer, consent and audit trail from scratch
Turning labs and records (including PDFs) into AI insights for its chat-based primary care
Prescription, payment, EHR sync and refill workflows for a virtual primary care service
Keeping patients inside its own branded app while it integrates with outside labs, imaging and pharmacies
Margin pressure on a roughly $50 per employee per month model, so a per-member data and AI cost needs to be justified

1735612732.summary: Mochi Health Corp is a San Francisco telehealth company founded in 2022. It started in medical weight loss with GLP-1s, both compounded and brand-name such as Zepbound, and runs a three-sided marketplace where patients choose their own provider and an independent pharmacy and see prices up front. It has since added hair loss, skincare, longevity, mental health, menopause and continuous glucose monitoring. Membership is $79/mo without insurance ($49/mo on a 12-month plan) or from $17/mo with insurance. A July 2026 article cites the company's own claim of more than 500,000 patients served.
1735612732.fit: Mochi is in the right space (GLP-1 telehealth, pharmacy fulfillment, lab panels from $26, longevity), but it is a large, cash-flow-positive platform. It already has its own iOS and Android app, has hired for a Head of Product, and runs its own pharmacy marketplace. A white-label app engine probably duplicates what it has built, and $8 per member per month across hundreds of thousands of patients would be a big cost next to building in-house. The most realistic way in is a module: AI that reads lab PDFs and turns them into health scores and insights, FHIR/EHR data sharing for its longevity, CGM and menopause lines, or a referral/channel deal that offers Connect to the independent pharmacies on its marketplace (the network grew from 10 to 33 pharmacies in one quarter).
pain_points: Turning results from its own lab panels (from $26) into personalized insights and coaching at scale
Moving data between many independent practices, a growing pharmacy network and outside EHRs using FHIR
Adding nine-plus care categories (longevity, menopause, CGM) without having to rebuild the data and AI stack for each
Compliance scrutiny: Eli Lilly patent suit reported ongoing, and a past pharmacy partner (Aequita) was suspended, which raises the value of consent tracking and audit trails
Trustpilot reviewers complain about rushed visits and slow support, which automated coaching and insights could ease

web-ivim-health.summary: Ivím Health is a physician-led U.S. virtual care company, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, that runs individualized GLP-1 weight-loss programs. It prescribes compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide as well as branded Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound, and has expanded into hormone health, longevity, sleep and recovery. It sells to consumers directly and to employers through Ivim at Work. It reports 470K+ patients served and about 100 board-certified providers, with peptide therapies listed as 'coming soon'.
web-ivim-health.fit: Ivim works in the same areas as our client MyWellness App: GLP-1, hormones, peptides and longevity. But it is a large, established player that already runs its own iOS and Android app (com.ivim.health) and its own medication workflow, so it doesn't need a white-label app and will be hard to win. The best opening is the gap in its stack. A user review says the app has no access to labs, and home testing is only listed as a planned feature. Our AI that reads lab PDFs and turns them into scores and coaching, plus FHIR/EHR sync for its hormone, peptide and corporate programs, could fill that gap. At its patient volume, $8 per member per month is a large contract, so it's worth exploring. Expect build-vs-buy pushback from an in-house product team.
pain_points: No lab data in the app: a user review says there is no access to labs, and home testing is only 'planned'
Launching peptide and hormone programs, which need lab-driven dosing and monitoring at scale
Weekly dose-adjustment check-ins with about 100 providers: AI insights and coaching could take some of that load off clinicians
Corporate program (Ivim at Work) likely needs consented, auditable health data and outcome reporting for employers
App reviews mention bugs, and Telehealth Ally reviews mention slower support around month three, which points to engagement and retention pressure
